title: Add missing at-since in AdministrativeMonitor
category: feature
requirement: '## Context


  The AdministrativeMonitor API recently gained manager-aware permission helpers, but its Javadoc still does not say which Jenkins version introduced them.


  ## Desired outcome


  The API documentation should identify the correct release so plugin developers can make versioned compatibility decisions.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The behavior of administrative monitors is unchanged, but the new monitor permission helpers have explicit `@since` metadata.

  '
=============== agent-protocols-config-removal
title: Removing configurability of `Jenkins.agentProtocols`
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator should not have to manually curate the list of built-in inbound agent protocols in the global security screen, because that configuration can drift away from the supported transport set and create confusion about what Jenkins actually allows.


  ## Desired outcome

  Jenkins should stop treating built-in agent protocols as an administrator-managed security setting and should instead expose the supported protocol set directly from core. The configuration UI and backing APIs should no longer offer agent protocol toggles that imply these built-in transports can be selectively disabled there.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The global security configuration no longer presents agent protocol selection as an editable admin setting, Jenkins reports the supported built-in protocols from core without relying on saved UI state, and upgrading preserves working agent connectivity without a manual protocol reconfiguration step.

  '
=============== atomicfilewriter-temp-names
title: Simplify AtomicFileWriter and use clearer temporary file names
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins operator writing critical configuration files expects atomic writes to stay dependable and the resulting logs to be readable when the filesystem does not support true atomic moves, but the current implementation produces obscure temporary names and noisy duplicate failure reporting.


  ## Desired outcome

  `AtomicFileWriter` should create clearer temporary file names derived from the destination path and should remember after the first `AtomicMoveNotSupportedException` that the platform requires a non-atomic fallback. =============== buildhistory-refresh-all-pages
title: '[JENKINS-73613] refresh buildhistory widget in all cases'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  The build history widget only refreshes reliably on the first page of results, so users looking at older pages can miss renamed builds, description changes, deletions, or updated running-build state until they manually reload.


  ## Desired outcome


  Build history should refresh whenever the page becomes active again and should keep the user on the same slice of history instead of snapping back to the top.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The widget refreshes on window focus, updates while viewing older pages, and preserves the current pagination context when reloading the build list.

  '
=============== buildwithparameters-303-redirects
title: '[JENKINS-66105] Allow follow redirects to work after 303 from `buildWithParameters`'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Some API clients trigger parameterized builds and then follow the redirect returned by `buildWithParameters`, but today a 303 chain can land on a queue item URL that is not useful to generic HTTP clients.


  ## Desired outcome


  Following the redirect from `buildWithParameters` should end on a stable queue item endpoint that both human operators and automation can consume.


  ## Acceptance signals


  A client that follows the initial 201 and later 303 response reaches a 200 response, and the queue item landing page points callers to `api/json?tree=cancelled,executable[url]` for status details.

  '
=============== cli-websocket-handshake-errors
title: Friendlier handling of `DeploymentHandshakeException` from CLI in `-webSocket` mode
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Users invoking the Jenkins CLI in `-webSocket` mode get an unhelpful failure when the WebSocket handshake is rejected, which makes authentication and reverse-proxy issues hard to diagnose.


  ## Desired outcome


  A handshake failure should tell the user what HTTP status came back and surface the response headers that matter for debugging.


  ## Acceptance signals


  On a rejected handshake the CLI prints `CLI handshake failed with status code 401`, includes headers such as `Server: Jetty` when available, and exits with status 15 instead of a generic stack trace.

  '
=============== command-palette-header-guard
title: '`headerCommandPaletteButton` undefined when `JenkinsHeader` not loaded'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins page that does not render the standard `JenkinsHeader` should still be allowed to load frontend assets safely, but the Command Palette initializer currently assumes the header button exists and crashes on layouts that omit it.


  ## Desired outcome

  The Command Palette frontend should detect when `headerCommandPaletteButton` is absent and simply skip initialization on that page. Pages without `JenkinsHeader` should remain fully usable instead of failing because the palette tried to bind to a missing control.


  ## Acceptance signals

  On layouts without the standard header, the page loads without JavaScript errors, the palette code exits early when `headerCommandPaletteButton` is missing, and pages that do include the header keep the normal Command Palette behavior.

  '
=============== command-palette-icons
title: Add icons to Command Palette
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins user searching from the Command Palette needs enough visual context to distinguish jobs, users, views, agents, and other results at a glance, but the current results list is text-only and forces people to infer the target type from the name alone.


  ## Desired outcome

  Search results returned to the Command Palette should include both an `icon` and a `type` so the frontend can render the right symbol for each result class. Jobs should expose meaningful status-based icons, and the palette should present those icons consistently across the different result types Jenkins exports.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Command Palette result payloads include `icon` and `type`, jobs surface a status-derived search icon, and users can visually distinguish result categories in the palette without opening each match first.

  '
=============== command-palette-ui-refinement
title: Refine Command Palette UI
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins user opening the Command Palette expects it to feel responsive and polished, but the current dialog can show awkward loading flicker, abrupt closing behavior, and visual rough edges that make the interaction feel unfinished.


  ## Desired outcome

  The Command Palette should load results with smoother spinner timing, cleaner open-and-close animation, and more consistent spacing and visual treatment so it feels like a first-class navigation surface. The interface should preserve existing search behavior while improving the perceived responsiveness of searching and dismissing the palette.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The loading spinner appears only when searches take long enough to warrant it, closing the palette uses a deliberate transition instead of an abrupt disappearance, and the updated palette styling reads as a polished UI refinement rather than a functional regression.

  '
=============== contextmenu-from-compatibility
title: '[JENKINS-73785] Restore `ContextMenu#from` with `StaplerRequest`/`Response` args'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Some plugins and adjunct code still call the older `ContextMenu#from` overload that accepts `StaplerRequest` and `StaplerResponse`, and that compatibility path disappeared during the newer request-type migration.


  ## Desired outcome


  Restore the legacy overload so existing integrations continue to build and run while the ecosystem migrates to the new request types.


  ## Acceptance signals


  `ContextMenu#from(ModelObjectWithContextMenu, StaplerRequest, StaplerResponse)` is available again and delegates to the newer request and response implementation instead of forcing every caller to migrate immediately.

  '
=============== deprecate-administrativemonitor-permission
title: Deprecate AdministrativeMonitor#getRequiredPermission
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Plugin authors still see `AdministrativeMonitor.getRequiredPermission()` as the obvious extension point even though newer permission-check helpers provide the safer contract Jenkins now expects.


  ## Desired outcome


  The older permission getter should remain available for compatibility but be clearly deprecated in favor of `checkRequiredPermission()` and `hasRequiredPermission()`.


  ## Acceptance signals


  Existing monitors continue to load, but developers are guided toward the newer helper methods instead of treating `getRequiredPermission()` as the preferred contract.

  '
=============== deprecate-subtask-getlastbuilton
title: Deprecating `SubTask.getLastBuiltOn`
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Queue scheduling still exposes `SubTask.getLastBuiltOn` even though Jenkins no longer relies on it in a meaningful way, which encourages plugin authors to depend on stale behavior.


  ## Desired outcome


  Mark this API as deprecated and communicate that it is no longer part of the supported scheduling contract, without changing how queued work is assigned or how builds run today.


  ## Acceptance signals


  Existing callers still compile and run, the deprecated entry points remain available for compatibility, and normal build execution behavior stays unchanged.

  '
=============== descriptor-newinstance-httpresponse
title: Tolerate `HttpResponse` thrown from `Descriptor.newInstance`
category: feature
requirement: '## Context


  Some descriptors intentionally abort instantiation by throwing an `HttpResponse`, for example to redirect or return a structured form response, but Jenkins currently risks wrapping that control flow as an internal instantiation failure.


  ## Desired outcome


  Descriptor creation should let intentional `HttpResponse` escapes propagate normally instead of turning them into linkage-style errors.


  ## Acceptance signals


  If `Descriptor.newInstance` encounters an exception that is also an `HttpResponse`, Jenkins preserves that response behavior; only true instantiation failures are wrapped and logged as such.

  '

=============== detached-plugin-cache
title: Use detached plugins as a cache for the Update Center
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Initial setup and plugin installation can spend unnecessary time downloading plugin files that Jenkins already ships as detached plugins.


  ## Desired outcome


  Jenkins should treat detached plugins as a best-effort cache for Update Center downloads so setup is faster when the bundled copy already matches the expected checksums.


  ## Acceptance signals


  If a matching detached plugin is already available, Jenkins installs from that cached file instead of the network; if validation or lookup fails, installation falls back to the normal download path without user-visible breakage.

  '
=============== detached-plugin-origin-logging
title: Note the plugin responsible for loading a detached plugin
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  When Jenkins auto-loads a detached plugin to satisfy an implied dependency, the current logging does not say which plugin caused that dependency to be pulled in.


  ## Desired outcome


  Operators should be able to see the originating plugin in the log message so dependency resolution is easier to audit.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The detached-plugin log line names both the detached plugin being loaded and the source plugin that required it.

  '
=============== disable-yui-default
title: '[JENKINS-73539] Disable YUI by default'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator upgrading the UI stack should get the YUI-free experience by default, because keeping the legacy library enabled unless someone opts in slows the transition and leaves obsolete dependencies active longer than necessary.


  ## Desired outcome

  The `RemoveYuiUserExperimentalFlag` should default to enabled so Jenkins removes YUI from pages unless an administrator explicitly opts back out through the `jenkins.model.experimentalflags.RemoveYuiUserExperimentalFlag.defaultValue` system property. Pages that no longer rely on YUI, including the old debug log reader hook, should continue to load without that library being initialized.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Fresh and upgraded controllers default to the YUI-removed path, administrators can still override the default with the `jenkins.model.experimentalflags.RemoveYuiUserExperimentalFlag.defaultValue` system property, and pages no longer initialize the legacy YUI debug log reader by default.

  '
=============== dosaferestart-compatibility
title: '[JENKINS-73838] Compatibility for `Jenkins#doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest, String)`'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Older callers still invoke `Jenkins#doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest, String)`, and the newer request-type migration should not break those integrations abruptly.


  ## Desired outcome


  Keep a compatibility overload for the old safe-restart signature while steering new development toward the `StaplerRequest2` form.


  ## Acceptance signals


  `Jenkins#doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest, String)` remains available as a deprecated bridge and delegates correctly to the newer safe-restart implementation.

  '
=============== dosaferestart-lts-backport
title: Backporting for 2.479.1 (part 4)
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Plugin or integration code that still calls the deprecated `doSafeRestart` overloads may pass a null request object in compatibility scenarios, and Jenkins currently throws before the restart flow can be delegated to the newer implementation.


  ## Desired outcome

  The deprecated `doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest)` and `doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest, String)` entry points should remain tolerant of `null` and forward that call through to the modern restart path without crashing. =============== flightrecorder-buffer-size
title: Reduce default size of diagnostic buffer for `FlightRecorderInputStream` from 1MiB to 1KiB
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator debugging CLI remoting failures needs the diagnostic ring buffer to preserve enough recent bytes to explain protocol corruption, but the current recorder is too small and can lose the context needed to troubleshoot intermittent failures.


  ## Desired outcome

  `FlightRecorderInputStream` should keep a larger default capture window and continue to make that size configurable through the `hudson.remoting.FlightRecorderInputStream.BUFFER_SIZE` system property. When CLI protocol parsing fails, the diagnostic output should retain enough recent traffic to make the corruption actionable.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The default recorder keeps a substantially larger recent byte history, operators can still override it with the `hudson.remoting.FlightRecorderInputStream.BUFFER_SIZE` property, and CLI corruption logs include enough buffered data to diagnose the failure instead of truncating the useful context.

  '
=============== heterolist-scroll-into-view
title: scroll fields from added hetero-list entry into viewport
category: feature
requirement: '## Context


  When a user adds a new hetero-list entry containing many fields, Jenkins may leave the newly added content partly off-screen, forcing manual scrolling before the user can continue.


  ## Desired outcome


  The form should automatically bring the newly added block into view in a browser-native way, including tall entries that extend beyond the viewport.


  ## Acceptance signals


  After adding an entry, the relevant fields are scrolled into view instead of being hidden below the fold, and the behavior works without relying on the old YUI viewport helpers.

  '
=============== idiomatic-python-style
title: Follow idiomatic Python coding style
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  The small Python maintenance script in this repository does not follow the project’s current Python style, which makes future edits noisier than they need to be.


  ## Desired outcome


  Align the script with idiomatic Python naming and environment checks without changing what the tool does.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The script behaves the same as before, but contributors see standard Python-style names and CI detection logic when they maintain it.

  '
=============== inbound-agent-websocket-default
title: Add -webSocket option by default when creating an inbound agent
category: feature
requirement: '## Context


  The Jenkins UI still generates inbound agent launch commands that omit WebSocket mode unless the user notices and adds it manually, even though WebSocket is the safer default for many modern installations and reverse-proxy setups.


  ## Desired outcome


  The generated inbound-agent command should include WebSocket mode by default so new agents start with the recommended connection mode.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The launch snippet produced for an inbound agent includes `-webSocket` even when the user has not toggled an extra option.

  '
=============== inbound-remoting-version-bypass
title: '[JENKINS-73467] No facility to try unsupported Remoting versions when using inbound agents'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context


  Some administrators intentionally allow older inbound remoting clients during upgrades, but WebSocket inbound agents still advertise the minimum supported version in a way that blocks those transitional rollouts.


  ## Desired outcome


  When the unsupported-remoting escape hatch is enabled, inbound agents connecting over WebSocket should be able to attempt the connection instead of being rejected up front by the version header.


  ## Acceptance signals


  If `SlaveComputer.ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_REMOTING_VERSIONS` is true, the WebSocket agent endpoint no longer sends the minimum-version header that preemptively blocks the agent; otherwise the existing safeguard remains in place.

  '
=============== item-creation-error-message
title: Fix error message when creation of item by type is prohibited
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context


  When Jenkins blocks creation of an item or view type for permission reasons, the error message includes a malformed permission path that repeats internal permission text and confuses administrators.


  ## Desired outcome


  The denial should name the missing permission and target type cleanly so the user understands what access is required.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The message format reads as `Job/Create/<type>` or `View/Create/<type>` without the duplicated permission token that was previously appended.

  '
=============== item-deletion-preflight-hook
title: '`ItemListener.onCheckDelete` & `ItemDeletion.cancelBuildsInProgress`'
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Plugins sometimes need to veto deletion before Jenkins starts canceling queue items or interrupting running builds, but the current deletion flow does not offer a dedicated preflight hook.


  ## Desired outcome


  Item deletion should expose a pre-delete extension point and centralize the logic that cancels in-flight work, while keeping the observable deletion safeguards the same.


  ## Acceptance signals


  `ItemListener.onCheckDelete(Item)` runs before deletion work starts and can stop the operation, `ItemDeletion.cancelBuildsInProgress` owns the build-cancellation behavior, and users still see the same protection against deleting items with builds that cannot be stopped cleanly.

  '
=============== javadoc-api-version-markers
title: Update version numbers of new APIs in Javadoc
category: feature
requirement: '## Context


  Recent public Jenkins APIs were added with placeholder or inaccurate version markers, which makes it harder for plugin developers to know when they can rely on them.


  ## Desired outcome


  The Javadoc for the newly introduced APIs should report the correct released version without changing runtime behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The affected public APIs keep the same names and semantics, but their `@since` documentation points to the correct release.

  '
=============== jenkins-load-view-recovery
title: Recover views after error in `Jenkins.load`
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator reloading configuration from disk expects a failed reload to leave the current view layout intact, but an exception during unmarshal can corrupt the in-memory view list and even leave `primaryView` in a broken recursive state.


  ## Desired outcome

  If configuration reload fails partway through, Jenkins should restore the original `views` collection and `primaryView` before rethrowing the error so the running controller remains navigable. Administrators should get the reload failure, but not lose access to their existing view configuration because of that failed attempt.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A reload failure does not wipe or corrupt the current view list, `primaryView` is restored to the pre-reload value instead of remaining null or recursive, and the controller stays usable after the failed reload while still surfacing the original error.

  '
=============== jetty-12-ee8-upgrade
title: '[JENKINS-73130] Upgrade core from Jetty 10.x to 12.x (EE 8)'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Jenkins needs the Jetty 12 EE8 upgrade to stay on supported infrastructure, but operators and plugin developers cannot absorb a server upgrade that silently breaks uploads, WebSocket settings, or existing compatibility knobs.


  ## Desired outcome


  The runtime should move to Jetty 12 EE8 while preserving established Jenkins behavior and keeping existing multipart tuning properties usable during the transition.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The WebSocket provider honors `jenkins.websocket.idleTimeout`, non-WebSocket requests are still rejected cleanly, and the legacy multipart property names `RequestImpl.FILEUPLOAD_MAX_FILES`, `RequestImpl.FILEUPLOAD_MAX_FILE_SIZE`, and `RequestImpl.FILEUPLOAD_MAX_SIZE` continue to map to the new `MultipartFormDataParser` limits.

  '

=============== keyboard-scroll-selection
title: Fix scrolling with keyboard
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins user navigating Command Palette results with the keyboard expects arrow-key movement to keep the selected item visible, but the current scroll helper can miss cases where the selected element is undefined and keyboard navigation becomes unreliable.


  ## Desired outcome

  Keyboard-driven navigation should tolerate the absence of a selected item and only try to scroll when a real selection exists. The Command Palette should continue to wire keyboard handling only while it is open so arrow-key navigation stays smooth instead of tripping over an uninitialized selection.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Using the keyboard to move through Command Palette results no longer throws or stalls when nothing is selected yet, scrolling resumes once an item is actually selected, and navigation remains scoped to the palette while it is open.

  '
=============== lifecycle-boot-failure
title: '`Lifecycle.onBootFailure`'
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Alternate Jenkins lifecycle implementations can react to restart and shutdown events, but they are not told when the controller fails during boot.


  ## Desired outcome


  Lifecycle providers should receive an explicit boot-failure callback so environments that rely on process supervision or auto-restart can handle startup failures intentionally.


  ## Acceptance signals


  A failed startup calls `Lifecycle.onBootFailure(BootFailure)`, and lifecycles such as the exit-based implementation can respond by restarting or terminating according to their policy.

  '
=============== lts-24793-zip-installer
title: Backporting for 2.479.3 LTS (part 3)
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator configuring a zip-based tool installer may point it at a local filesystem URI or another non-HTTP(S) source, but the current validation rejects those values even when they resolve to a valid path.


  ## Desired outcome

  The LTS line should accept non-HTTP(S) installer URIs whenever `Path.of(uri)` succeeds, while still rejecting malformed values with the existing validation path. Administrators using local or path-backed tool archives should be able to save those configurations again in the backported release.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Valid non-HTTP(S) URIs that resolve through `Path.of(uri)` are accepted, malformed non-HTTP(S) values still fail validation, and zip-based tool installers using local URIs work again on the backported line.

  '

title: '[JENKINS-73563] Create a `jenkins-button` instead of a YUI button in `makeButton`'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Jenkins wants to phase out YUI-era buttons, but many pages still call `makeButton`, so a full rewrite of every caller is not practical at once.


  ## Desired outcome


  `makeButton` should create a standard `jenkins-button` element while keeping just enough compatibility for legacy callers to continue working during the migration.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The replacement control renders as a `jenkins-button`, primary and secondary styling are preserved, `data-*` attributes survive the conversion, and callers can still use the returned wrapper to toggle disabled state and locate the enclosing form.

  '

title: Allow administrative monitors to be displayed for users with `Overall/MANAGE` permission
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Jenkins administrators with `Overall/MANAGE` but not `Overall/SYSTEM_READ` can still be responsible for day-to-day controller health, yet some administrative monitors disappear entirely for them.


  ## Desired outcome


  Some monitors should be able to opt into manager visibility so operators with `Overall/MANAGE` can see and act on those notices without granting broader read access to the whole system.


  ## Acceptance signals


  A monitor that relaxes its gate through `getRequiredPermission()`, `checkRequiredPermission()`, and `hasRequiredPermission()` can appear in the administrative monitors area for a manager-only user, while monitors that still require higher permission remain hidden.

  '

  ## Acceptance signals

=============== offline-status-persistence
title: '[JENKINS-30101][JENKINS-30175] Simplify persistence design for temporarily offline status'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  The temporary offline state for an agent currently lives partly on the `Computer`, which makes the status fragile across reconnects, controller restarts, and node reconfiguration even though operators expect that intent to persist with the node itself.


  ## Desired outcome


  Temporary offline state and its message should be owned by the `Node`, while compatibility entry points on `Computer` and the CLI continue to behave as operators expect.


  ## Acceptance signals


  Taking an agent offline through the CLI records an `OfflineCause.ByCLI`, `getTemporaryOfflineCauseReason()` reports the persisted message, existing compatibility setters still work, and a missing target still reports `ERROR: No such agent "never_created" exists.`.

  '
=============== os-eol-warning-date
title: '[JENKINS-73845] Fix OperatingSystemEndOfLifeAdminMonitor endOfLifeDate displayed on first warning day'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator who sees the operating-system end-of-life warning on the very first day it should appear expects the banner to report the real end-of-life date immediately, but the monitor can show the wrong value on that first warning day.


  ## Desired outcome

  `OperatingSystemEndOfLifeAdminMonitor` should activate on the first warning day and expose `getEndOfLifeDate()` as the actual configured end-of-life date for the matched operating system, not a placeholder or later-updated value. Administrators should be able to trust the date shown in the warning as soon as the banner first appears.


  ## Acceptance signals

  On the warning start date, the monitor activates for the matching OS, `getEndOfLifeDate()` returns the configured end-of-life date right away, and the banner shows the same date administrators are expected to plan around.

  '
=============== peepholepermalink-cache-extension
title: '`PeepholePermalink.Cache`'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Plugin developers who customize permalink lookup need a supported way to replace the cache behind `PeepholePermalink`, and Jenkins operators expect nearest-build navigation to keep returning the correct build around gaps created by deleted runs. The current implementation hard-codes the cache and leaves some lookup semantics implicit.


  ## Desired outcome

  `PeepholePermalink` should expose its cache as an extension point through `PeepholePermalink.Cache`, with persisted entries using the existing `id + " " + (build == null ? -1 : build.getNumber())` storage shape so alternate cache implementations remain compatible. At the same time, nearest-build and nearest-old-build resolution should preserve the exact numeric behavior Jenkins expects when build numbers are missing.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Plugins can supply a `PeepholePermalink.Cache` implementation without replacing permalink logic wholesale, persisted cache entries stay compatible with the `id + " " + (build == null ? -1 : build.getNumber())` format, and nearest-build navigation returns the documented builds before and after gaps caused by deletions.

  '
=============== pipeline-deletion-lts-backport
title: Backporting for 2.479.1 (part 2)
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator deleting a Pipeline job expects Jenkins to stop waiting once the build that originally blocked deletion is no longer the active executable, but the current deletion loop can keep interrupting stale executor state and leave job removal hanging longer than necessary.


  ## Desired outcome

  Job deletion should track whether an executor is still active on the same executable before continuing to wait on it. If the executor is no longer active, or has already moved on, Jenkins should stop treating it as a blocker so deleting the job can complete promptly after the running work really ends.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Deleting a job with in-flight work no longer depends on repeatedly interrupting stale executor state, Jenkins stops waiting for executors that are no longer active on the original executable, and job deletion finishes once the genuinely active work is gone.

  '
=============== plugin-download-source-url
title: Show plugin source URL when downloading it
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  When Jenkins downloads a plugin during installation or upgrade, operators can see the plugin name in logs but not the exact source URL, which makes mirror issues and provenance checks harder.


  ## Desired outcome


  Download logging should show the concrete plugin URL Jenkins is fetching so administrators can diagnose slow or unexpected sources without extra debugging.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The download message names the plugin and includes the full source URL that Jenkins is using for that artifact.

  '
=============== prettier-formatting-errors
title: Fix Prettier errors
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Jenkins core maintainers need the frontend codebase to stay formatted consistently so automated checks remain green and future UI changes are easier to review. The current issue is formatting drift rather than a user-visible defect.


  ## Desired outcome

  The affected frontend script should be brought back into Prettier-compliant form without changing runtime behavior, public APIs, or page behavior. This is tooling-oriented cleanup in a user-facing file, so observable Jenkins behavior must remain exactly the same.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Prettier-style checks pass for the touched script, the diff is formatting-only, and users and plugins observe no behavior change after the cleanup.

  '
=============== printstacktrace-logging-cleanup
title: Clean up a few plain `e.printStackTrace()` calls
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context


  A few remaining plain `e.printStackTrace()` calls bypass Jenkins logging conventions and make failures harder to route, filter, or diagnose in production.


  ## Desired outcome


  Replace those ad hoc prints with normal logger-based reporting without changing the surrounding control flow.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The affected failure paths still behave the same for users, but their diagnostics are emitted through Jenkins loggers rather than raw stack traces on stderr.

  '
=============== remove-rekeysecretadminmonitor
title: '[JENKINS-73597] Remove `RekeySecretAdminMonitor` and related resources'
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context


  Jenkins still carries the old `RekeySecretAdminMonitor` and its supporting code even though the security migration it was built for is long past and operators should no longer be managing that workflow.


  ## Desired outcome


  Remove this obsolete administrative monitor and its related implementation so the security surface is smaller and the manage page no longer advertises a dead-end maintenance task.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The `RekeySecretAdminMonitor` UI and backend are gone, while ordinary secret storage and startup behavior continue to work without any replacement rekey flow.

  '
=============== replace-ant-zip
title: Reduce usage of Ant
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins operator downloading archived workspaces or artifacts as ZIP files expects the generated archives to remain compatible while core gradually sheds legacy Ant dependencies.


  ## Desired outcome

  Jenkins should produce those ZIP responses using the standard `java.util.zip` classes instead of Ant’s ZIP implementation, while preserving the current archive contents and default charset behavior. This is internal maintenance work in a user-facing path, so the download experience should stay the same.


  ## Acceptance signals

  ZIP downloads from directory browsing and virtual file paths continue to open correctly after the dependency swap, Jenkins no longer relies on Ant ZIP classes in those code paths, and users do not observe changed archive contents or broken downloads as a result of the cleanup.

  '
=============== resource-url-escape-hatch
title: '[JENKINS-73422] Add escape hatch for Authenticated user access to Resource URL'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context


  The resource-domain hardening blocks authenticated users from accessing resource URLs, which is the secure default, but some administrators need a temporary emergency escape hatch while they unwind dependent workflows.


  ## Desired outcome


  Preserve the secure default while allowing a deliberate opt-out that re-enables authenticated access to the resource domain.


  ## Acceptance signals


  Authenticated requests stay blocked by default, but setting `ResourceDomainRootAction.ALLOW_AUTHENTICATED_USER` allows those requests to succeed again without changing anonymous-resource behavior.

  '

  ## Desired outcome

  Creating an item through the standard `createItem` endpoint should behave like a normal item-creation operation, not like an implicit “add to current view” action. A newly created job should exist in Jenkins, but the default view should not be populated as a side effect of that REST call.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A Jenkins administrator creating a job through the REST API expects that operation to create the item and leave view membership unchanged unless they explicitly add it to a view, and extension code that derives caller information should still resolve the initiating class correctly on modern JDKs.


  ## Desired outcome

The item-creation endpoint should still be handled as a proper POST operation.


  ## Acceptance signals

That cleanup added churn without improving the real safety boundary.


  ## Desired outcome

  '

This is a developer-facing API improvement, not a change in how standard update sites behave for administrators.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A subclass of `UpdateSite` can call `updateData(String json, boolean signatureCheck)` without reflection or copy-pasted logic, the shared parsing and signature-check flow remains intact, and standard Jenkins update-site behavior stays the same.

  '

category: other

  Plugin developers and advanced integrators need to know which `User` APIs are still experimental before they depend on them, but `User.reload()` currently looks like an ordinary stable entry point even though it is not meant to be treated that way yet.


  ## Desired outcome

  `User.reload()` should be explicitly marked as Beta API so consumers understand that the method is available but not yet part of Jenkins’ stable long-term contract. This is a contract-clarity change rather than a behavioral one.


  ## Acceptance signals

  '

  '

category: bugfix

  '
